title: Churros with Chocolate Sauce
subtitle: Crisp fried dough fingers with a thick, dark chocolate dipping sauce
excerpt: Light, crisp churros made from a choux-style dough, fried until golden and rolled in cinnamon sugar, served with a thick chocolate dipping sauce.
sourceNotes: A classic Spanish street food and breakfast treat, traditionally served at churrerias and during festivals.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dough can be made up to 2 hours ahead and kept at room temperature. Fry just before serving.

glossaryTerms.definition: A dough made by cooking flour in boiling water before adding eggs, giving a light and hollow result when fried.

content.text: This recipe serves 4 and takes about 40 minutes. The churros dough comes together in one saucepan and the chocolate sauce in a second. Make the sauce first so it is ready when the churros come out of the oil, which is when they are at their best.

The dough needs to be piped or spooned directly into hot oil. A piping bag with a star nozzle gives the classic ridged shape, but two spoons work perfectly well. Oil temperature matters: too cool and the churros absorb oil and go heavy; too hot and they colour before the inside cooks through. Aim for 180C and use a thermometer if you have one.

items.prepNote: enough to fill the pan 5cm deep, for frying

content.text: Make the chocolate sauce first. Whisk together the milk, plain flour, honey and cinnamon in a small saucepan until the flour is dissolved with no lumps. Set over a medium heat and stir constantly for 4 to 5 minutes until the sauce thickens to the consistency of a light custard. Keep warm over the lowest heat, stirring occasionally.

Make the churro dough. Bring 240ml of water to a rolling boil in a medium saucepan with the butter. Add the flour all at once and beat vigorously with a wooden spoon over the heat for 1 to 2 minutes until the dough pulls cleanly away from the sides and forms a smooth ball.

Remove from the heat and leave to cool for 3 minutes. Add the beaten eggs in two additions, beating well between each until fully incorporated. The dough should be smooth, glossy and fall off the spoon in a thick ribbon.
Mix the caster sugar and cinnamon in a shallow bowl. Set aside. Heat the vegetable oil in a wide pan over a medium-high heat to 180C.

Spoon or pipe 8cm lengths of dough directly into the hot oil, snipping off with scissors if piping. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp. Do not crowd the pan. Drain briefly on kitchen paper.
Roll the hot churros immediately in the cinnamon sugar. Serve at once with the warm dipping sauce alongside.

items.problem: The churros are greasy and heavy rather than crisp
items.solution: The oil was not hot enough. Always check the temperature before frying and let it recover between batches.

items.problem: The dough will not hold its shape and spreads in the oil
items.solution: The dough was not cooked long enough in the pan after the flour was added. Cook it until it forms a firm ball that pulls away completely from the sides.
Whisk the flour into the cold milk thoroughly before applying any heat. If lumps form while cooking, remove from the heat and whisk vigorously until smooth.

that gives them a light interior behind the crisp shell. They are best eaten the moment they leave the oil. They do not hold well, so make them in small batches and eat immediately. The dipping sauce here uses flour and honey for a thick, spoonable result that clings well.
